name: Fergus Mallory
languages: Irish (from his grandmother, mostly songs and curses)
equipment: Leather duster, black, too long for him, won at cards from a stage robber in Cheyenne
Army revolver (Colt single-action, .45), 6 rounds loaded, worn butt-forward
Coach gun (double-barrel, 12-gauge, sawn short), both barrels loaded, on a sling under the duster
Dynamite (4 sticks), wrapped in oilcloth in his saddlebag, with a coil of fuse and a box of blasting caps kept well away from it
A prospector's pick, a gold pan and a sack of ore samples, which are his excuse for being anywhere
Horse: Sullivan, a wiry blue roan, with a brand so artistically altered that even its first owner would not recognise it
Running iron, which is a hanging offence to carry in Wyoming, hidden in the lining of his saddle
A penny whistle and a pocket full of peppermints
features: Book Learning (Back East origin: advantage on Investigation checks to read documents such as deeds, contracts, ledgers, telegrams and forged papers; once per long rest, recall one useful fact about a law, process, science or history without a check; disadvantage on the first Riding or Survival check in front of strangers each day)

Dirty Fighting (Outlaw: once per turn, when he hits a creature that isn't ready, he deals an extra 1d6 damage of the weapon's type; a creature isn't ready if it is surprised, hasn't yet taken a turn in this combat, can't see him, or is prone, grappled, restrained or on a spooked horse; not part of the damage on his sheet)
Hard Riding (Outlaw: advantage on Riding checks in a chase he is fleeing; mounts and dismounts with 5 ft of movement; on each of his turns he can take a bonus action to Dash, Disengage or Hide)

Powder Man (Outlaw, 2nd level: lighting a fuse is part of the throw; his thrown explosives use save DC 13; he sets and fuses a charge in 1 minute instead of 10 with no chance of it going off early, and can cut a fuse to burn for any time from 1 round to an hour)

Trade: Rustler (Outlaw, 3rd level: he can move a herd of up to 50 head at a normal pace and leave a trail that needs a DC 20 Survival check to follow, and alters a brand with a running iron at advantage)

Color in the Creek (Prospector background: he tells good ore from bad without a check, knows claim law, finds a camp's assay office and claim jumpers within the hour, and has a dozen hiding places in the Red Breaks that nobody else knows)

personality.traits: I am charming, cheerful, generous and a thief, in roughly that order. I whistle when I am nervous and when I am happy, so nobody can tell. I never steal from anyone who cannot afford it, which in Wyoming narrows the field to about four men.
personality.ideals: A company that claims every blade of grass from here to Montana and owns three acres of it is the biggest rustler in the territory. I am only the most honest one.
personality.bonds: My horses, my hidden cabin in the Red Breaks, and the creek folk who have fed me for three years and never asked where the beef came from. Calvin Booker, who disapproves of me and would die before he let anyone hang me.
personality.flaws: I am a rustler, a real one, and everything the Association says about me is true. I would rather run than fight, and I have run out on people before. I am afraid of rope, very afraid, and I have good reason.

appearance: A wiry, wolfish, red-haired man of thirty with a freckled, much-broken nose, a wide crooked grin, bright green eyes and the restless hands of a card player. Black duster too long for him, a battered derby hat, a red neckerchief, and a blue roan horse with an imaginative brand.
backstory: Fergus Mallory was born in Philadelphia in 1856, the son of an Irish ironworker, went down the coal mines of Schuylkill County at twelve, and learned there to handle powder, to hate company stores and company police, and to keep his mouth shut. He left the coal country in a hurry in 1876, during a bad time for Irish miners who knew too much, and drifted west: a powder man in the Black Hills, a teamster, a faro dealer, a horse-breaker, a prospector who never found anything worth the name. He came to Bitter Creek in 1883 and discovered that the easiest money in Wyoming was the Company's unbranded calves and loose horses, and that the homesteaders would buy beef without asking questions. He has been stealing from the Bitter Creek Land & Cattle Company ever since, carefully, selling horses south in Colorado, and the Association has put $500 on his head and his name on the dead list. On the night of Sunday 18 April he was driving six of the Company's horses into the Red Breaks by moonlight, and from a ridge above the creek road he saw two riders going up toward the Narrows from Gilead: a long man on a bay that moved short on the near fore, and a boy. He has told no one. Who would believe a horse thief?

dmNotes.roleplaying: Mallory is the party's rogue: comic relief with real stakes, a witness nobody will believe, a guide to the Red Breaks, and the man with the dynamite. He is the red herring the Company would love to hang for Owen's murder, and a party working for the Company may be tempted; let the temptation be real. He saw the hangmen on the road on Sunday night and will tell a party that protects him or trusts him (corroboration for CLUES A3 and B1, from a witness the court will not like). In bk-scenario-003 his dynamite and his Powder Man specialty are the siege's wild card. He will not stand in a fight he thinks is lost unless someone he loves is in it; by the siege, that may include the party.
dmNotes.voice: A quick Philadelphia Irish patter, cheerful and self-mocking, full of terrible jokes, pet names ('darling', 'your honour', 'Sergeant' for Booker) and Irish songs half sung. Goes completely quiet and flat when he is frightened, and that is how you know.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: not hang. Secondary: keep his horses, his cabin and his friends. Tertiary, and he would deny it: be on the right side of something, once, for the whole of it.
dmNotes.secrets: He knows the Company's own tally man has been working homesteaders' brands into the Bar BC in a brush corral in a cedar draw off the Sage Flats; he found the corral and stole six of the 'Company' cattle back to their owners last autumn, which is the 'rustling' the Association most wants him for. He can lead the party to the corral (see bk-scenario-002). Second secret: the Association's $500 is for a different Fergus Mallory, a Montana horse thief who is dead; the description on the poster fits him only because the clerk copied it. Delfina Ochoa, if she is played, can find this out, and it is her choice what to do with it.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: delighted, flirtatious, and quietly measuring whether they will hang him. Toward Delfina Ochoa: he knows exactly who she is and why she came, and he flirts with her outrageously, because the alternative is running. Toward Calvin Booker: affectionate, a little in awe. Toward the Company: cheerful larceny. Toward Stroud: terror, covered with jokes. Toward Gideon Sayre: dislike he cannot explain; 'the man's never once looked me in the eye, and I'm a thief.'
